gaps.sentence: 'Don't be late again,' the coach told him. The coach told him ___ late again.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands: not to be, with the negative before the whole infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.

gaps.sentence: 'Please reconsider my application,' she wrote. She ___ them to reconsider her application.
gaps.explanation: A polite written request is reported with asked + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
gaps.explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.
